description:
## Context

QuickHeadlines on FreeBSD crashes after 1-2 days of uptime with
excessive memory growth (observed: 9GB VIRT after 1.5h; 4.3GB RSS
after 22h; full system crash after 1-2 days). The in-progress
investigation `quickhea-alz` confirmed EventBroadcaster was leaking
client references; that fix landed in the previous commit
(c1a067d0).

This epic enumerates the remaining suspected leak vectors based on a
code review. Each child task is a focused investigation + fix;
together they should bound RSS growth to a few hundred MB and
prevent the multi-day crash.

## Suspected leak vectors (by file/area)

1. **feed_fetcher_concurrent.cr** — per-feed inner fibers hold the
   feed config and result_channel until the fetch returns; with 100+
   feeds every 30 min, transient fiber-stack and captured-variable
   retention can add up. Also: channel.send on a closed channel is
   rescued, but the inner fiber still allocates fetch_result and any
   exception payloads before noticing.
2. **favicon_storage.cr @client_pool** — Hash(String, HTTP::Client)
   keyed by host. Each unique feed host adds a HTTP::Client (with its
   own socket pool) that is never removed. Grows unbounded as unique
   hosts are seen.
3. **actor.cr _actor_call_with_timeout_json** — every def_call
   allocates a fresh Channel(String).new(1). If the caller raises
   between send_message and receive, or under a 30s timeout, the
   channel + struct linger. With high call rates, this is hundreds of
   short-lived channels/min.
4. **socket_manager.cr writer fiber** — spawned per connection;
   relies on outgoing channel close to exit. A half-closed TCP socket
   that the runtime does not notice as closed? keeps the writer
   fiber spinning and holding conn + any pending broadcast payloads.
5. **string_pool.cr StringIntern eviction** — when MAX_POOL_SIZE is
   hit, the oldest half of the keys is removed but the interned
   strings may still be referenced by FeedData. Verify retention
   policy.
6. **gc_collector.cr** — maybe_collect only runs when refresh_all
   completes; if the supervisors run_timed_refresh skips due to
   memory-critical pressure, no GC happens until the next successful
   cycle. Add a wall-clock backstop (already a candidate in
   quickhea-hwp).
7. **refresh_supervisor.cr** — run_timed_refresh creates cancel_ch
   and completion_channel per cycle. On the timeout branch the
   worker fiber is not joined — it keeps running until it finishes
   internally and may retain large fetched_map.
8. **app_state_service.cr @memory_history** — capped at 500, OK.
9. **app_state_service.cr track_memory_usage** — minor off-by-one in
   the modulo check; not a leak. Note for cleanup.
10. **event_broadcaster.cr @@client_history** — capped at 1000, OK.

## Goals

- Identify the dominant leak(s) with measurements, not guesses.
- Cap all unbounded data structures in the long-lived paths
  (connections, fibers, actor channels, HTTP clients).
- Add forced GC + per-cycle heap snapshots so future leaks are
  diagnosable in 10 min, not 22 h.
- Keep QuickHeadlines stable on FreeBSD for >=7 days under nominal
  load with RSS under 1 GB.

## Acceptance

- Heap snapshots before/after each fix, RSS growth over 24 h < 100 MB
  on the same config as the FreeBSD production jail.
- All child tasks closed; bw sync clean.
- No new lints (ameba) and spec suite green.

## Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
  1[Add heap snapshot + RSS delta instrument] --> 2[Audit unbounded data structures]
  2 --> 3[Cap FaviconActor client pool]
  2 --> 4[Cap SocketManager writer fiber retention]
  2 --> 5[Cap actor reply channel lifetime]
  2 --> 6[Add periodic forced full GC backstop]
  3 --> 7[Long-running FreeBSD soak test 48h]
  4 --> 7
  5 --> 7
  6 --> 7
  1 --> 7
```
title: Memory leak investigation & fixes for FreeBSD 1-2 day crash
